title: Revealment and average complexity
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be invariant under a transitive action of coordinate permutations, and let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on $\{-1,1\}$. Then the infimum, over randomized decision trees computing $f$, of their revealment under the product input distribution with marginal $\pi$ equals the corresponding infimum of average query costs divided by $n$.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number of input coordinates
A Boolean function with sign-valued inputs and outputs
Invariance under a transitive action of coordinate permutations
A probability distribution on the sign alphabet
